cim_eredeti: Whilly Bermudez Of Ai Course 360 On How Artificial Intelligence Can Solve Business Problems
szoveg_eredeti:
For me, the exciting part isn’t replacing creativity with technology. It’s using technology to expand what creative people can accomplish.

In today’s technology-driven world, artificial intelligence has become an important tool for business success. But how can companies effectively use Ai to solve real challenges while maintaining ethical standards? To explore this subject, we spoke with Whilly Bermudez, an award-winning marketer and Ai Master Instructor, about how artificial intelligence is changing the way businesses operate, communicate, and grow.

As a part of this series, we had the pleasure to interview Whilly Bermudez.

Whilly Bermudez is an award-winning marketer, creative strategist, and Ai Master Instructor with over two decades of experience in marketing, advertising, and business innovation. Throughout his career, he has led more than 1,000 marketing and creative projects and earned over 100 industry awards and recognitions, including achievements in healthcare and technology marketing. As the founder of Ai Course 360, he focuses on teaching entrepreneurs, business owners, and professionals how to use artificial intelligence for marketing, content creation, automation, productivity, and business growth.

Thank you so much for joining us in this interview series! Before we dive into our discussion, our readers would love to get to know you a bit better. Can you share with us the backstory about what brought you to your specific career path in AI?

My background is actually in marketing, advertising, and creative strategy. I’ve spent more than two decades helping businesses develop brands, launch products, and connect with their audiences. Over the years, I’ve worked in several industries, including entertainment, hospitality, healthcare, and technology.

I’ve always been interested in technology and how it can improve the way we work. When artificial intelligence started becoming more accessible, I immediately saw its potential, particularly in marketing, advertising, and content creation.

I began experimenting with different Ai platforms, learning what they could do and figuring out how to incorporate them into actual business applications. What fascinated me most was that tasks that previously required significant time, resources, or specialized production teams could now be approached much more efficiently.

As I became more experienced with these tools, I realized there was a tremendous need for practical education. Many business owners were hearing about Ai but had absolutely no idea where to begin.

That’s what inspired me to create Ai Course 360. I wanted to develop a learning experience that teaches people how to use artificial intelligence in ways that are practical, understandable, and directly applicable to their businesses.

Can you share the most interesting story that happened to you since you started working with artificial intelligence?

One of the most interesting things has been seeing how much Ai has changed creative production.

I’ve spent years developing advertising campaigns, producing videos, and creating marketing content. Traditionally, bringing certain creative concepts to life could involve photographers, videographers, designers, editors, and significant production expenses.

When I started experimenting with Ai-generated visuals and video, I realized just how dramatically some of those processes could change.

I could take a creative concept, develop the script, explore different visual directions, and produce elements that would previously have required a much larger production effort.

But I also discovered something equally important. Ai doesn’t automatically make someone creative.

I’ve seen plenty of Ai-generated content that looks impressive at first glance but lacks originality, proper branding, or a clear message. The technology can produce something visually interesting without necessarily producing something effective.

That experience reinforced my belief that creative direction and professional judgment still matter tremendously.

For me, the exciting part isn’t replacing creativity with technology. It’s using technology to expand what creative people can accomplish.

Which three-character traits do you think were most instrumental to your success? Can you please share a story or example for each?

I would say curiosity, adaptability, and persistence.

Curiosity has always been a major part of my personality. I like understanding how things work, especially when I see an opportunity to improve an existing process. When I started exploring Ai, I didn’t limit myself to one platform. I experimented with image generation, video production, writing tools, automation, and different business applications. That curiosity helped me understand the technology beyond the basic features most people initially discover.

Adaptability has also been extremely important. My career started in traditional marketing and live entertainment promotions, and eventually expanded into digital marketing, healthcare technology, and artificial intelligence. Every one of those transitions required learning something new. I’ve always believed that if you want to remain relevant professionally, you have to be willing to evolve.

Persistence is the third. Anyone who works seriously with Ai knows that it doesn’t always produce the results you want. I’ve spent considerable time refining prompts, correcting visual details, and experimenting with different approaches to achieve a specific creative result. Sometimes the first output is terrible. You have to recognize what isn’t working and keep improving it.

Those three traits have helped me throughout my career, and they’re just as important when working with artificial intelligence.

Can you share a specific example of how you or your organization used AI to solve a major business challenge? What was the problem, and how did AI help address it?

One example comes from my professional experience in healthcare technology, particularly with a software platform called Navigator at Health Tech Global.

Healthcare organizations face significant financial and operational challenges. Hospitals, for example, have to manage expenses, procedures, patient cases, operational costs, and profitability across multiple departments.

Navigator uses artificial intelligence to analyze financial and operational information and help organizations forecast profitability over quarterly and annual periods.

The business challenge is making sense of large amounts of complicated information and turning that information into something useful for decision-makers.

My involvement was on the business and marketing side, helping communicate the platform’s capabilities and business value.

What I found particularly interesting was how Ai could support a highly complex industry by helping organizations better understand their financial outlook.

That experience demonstrated something important to me. Artificial intelligence isn’t limited to creating content or answering questions. It can also help organizations analyze complex business situations and make more informed decisions.

It’s one of the reasons I emphasize real business applications through Ai Course 360. The technology becomes much more valuable when people understand how to connect it to an actual problem.

What are some of the common misconceptions you’ve encountered about using AI in business? How do you address those misconceptions?

The biggest misconception is that Ai does all the work for you.

People sometimes think they can type a few words into an Ai platform and automatically receive a perfect result. Unfortunately, that’s not how it works, especially when you’re producing professional content or working on important business tasks.

The quality of the results depends on the instructions you provide, the information available, and your ability to evaluate what the technology produces.
